This is a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act").

The Petitioner, aggrieved by the compensation amount awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector vide Award No. 13/2008-09/SW relating to the acquisition of village Nangli Sakrawati for construction of 100 mtrs. sentences.text: 25. Per contra, the Respondent/Union of India has relied upon the Award (Ex. R1W1/1) and argued that the compensation awarded by the LAC is just and reasonable.

26. The land in question, situated in Village Nangli Sakrawati, was notified for acquisition under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, vide Notification dated 07.04.2006 (as corroborated by the judgment in R.C. Tehlan v. UOI, which pertains Digitally to the same acquisition).

The Ld. LAC assessed the market value based on the policy rates fixed by the Govt. of NCT of Delhi.

However, it is settled law that when evidence of bona fide sale transactions of the same village and proximate in time is available, the same should be preferred over government minimum rates which often lag behind the actual market trends.

28. The Petitioner has placed on record two sale deeds from the same village, Nangli Sakrawati,
executed in close proximity to the date of the Section 4 Notification (07.04.2006).
a. Ex. PW-1/2 (Sale Deed dated 14.11.2005): This sale deed was executed approximately 4 months and 24 days prior to the date of notification.
It pertains to the sale of a 1/3rd share in agricultural land measuring 8 Bighas and 10 Biswas for Rs. 28,00,000/-.

Rate Calculation: Rs. 28,00,000/- for 2.833 Bighas (approx.) = Rs. 9,88,240/- per Bigha (approx. Rs. 47,43,552/- per acre).
b. Ex. PW-1/1 (Sale Deed dated 24.04.2006): This sale deed was executed 17 days after the date of notification.
It pertains to land measuring 9 Bighas 06 Biswas for Rs. 48,00,000/-.
Rate Calculation: Rs. 48,00,000/- for 9.3 Bighas = Rs. 5,16,129/- per Bigha (approx. Rs. 24,77,419/- per acre).
29. Both sale deeds are genuine, registered documents pertaining to agricultural land in the same village.

sentences.text: Such variations are not uncommon in real estate transactions, but they necessitate a balanced approach to determine the fair market value.

30. The Petitioner has relied upon the judgment in R.C. Tehlan v. Union of India, LAC No. 35/2014,
decided by the Ld. ADJ-04, South West District, Dwarka Courts.

entities.text: R.C. Tehlan v. Union of India, LAC No. 35/2014
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A perusal of the said judgment reveals that:
a. It pertains to the same village (Nangli Sakrawati). b.

It involves the same Notification under Section 4 dated 07.04.2006.
c.
It involves the same public purpose (Construction of 100 Mtrs. Road).

d. Most importantly, the Court in R.C. Tehlan relied upon the exact same sale deeds (Ex. PW1/8 and Ex. PW1/9 in that case, which correspond to Ex. PW-1/2 and Ex. PW-1/1 in the present case) to determine the market value.

31. In R.C. Tehlan, the Court observed that since the date of notification (07.04.2006) falls between the dates of the two sale deeds (14.11.2005 and 24.04.2006), it is just and appropriate to take the average of the market values reflected in these two deeds.
Rate as per Sale Deed dated 14.11.2005 is Rs. 47,43,552/- per acre.
Rate as per Sale Deed dated 24.04.2006 is Rs. 24,77,419/- per acre.
Average Rate: (47,43,552 + 24,77,419) / 2 = Rs. 36,10,485/- per SUMIT DALAL acre.

The Court in R.C. Tehlan consequently fixed the market value at Rs. 36,10,485/- per acre (or Rs. 7,52,184.37 per Bigha).
32.

Judicial propriety and the principle of parity demand that owners of acquired lands under the same notification and in the same village for the same block of land should be awarded compensation at a uniform rate, unless there are distinct features distinguishing the lands.
In the present case, no evidence has been led by the Respondents to show that the Petitioner's land is inferior to the land involved in the R.C. Tehlan case or the lands covered by the sale deeds.

Nothing has been brought on record which may prove that the adjudication of the market value in R.C.
Tehlan has been set aside by the Hon'ble Superior Courts.

33. Therefore, adopting the reasoning and the computation arrived at in the case of R.C. Tehlan v.
Union of India, LAC No. 35/2014, which relied upon the very same evidence produced in this case, I hold that the fair market value of the acquired land in respect of Block A land as on the date of notification under Section 4 (i.e., 07.04.2006) was Rs. 36,10,485/- per acre.

Following the procedural requirements of the Act, the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as "LAC") passed Award No. 13/2008-09/SW on 30.03.2009, vide which the possession of the entire acquired land was taken over by the Government.
4. During the course of proceedings, it was brought to the notice of the Court that there was a dispute regarding the apportionment of compensation between various claimants to the acquired land i.e. land bearing Khasra No. 13//10 min (0-14),
13//11/1 min (1-2) and 11 min (0-8) total measuring 2 Bigha 4 Biswa situated in revenue estate of Village Nangli Sakrawati, Delhi and the dispute is under adjudication under Section 30-31 of the Act in LAC No. 40/2014, titled Union of India v. Gaon Sabha Nangli Sakrawati & Ors.
Specifically, there was a dispute as to whether the Petitioner was the absolute owner of the land or whether the Gaon Sabha had any interest therein.
Accordingly, on an application filed by the counsel for the Petitioner, with the consent of all parties, the Court by its order dated 05.09.2014 adjourned this reference petition sine die, with liberty for revival, pending the disposal of the SUMIT DALAL apportionment proceedings under Section 30-31 of the Land Acquisition Act.
In that judgment, it was held that although the Petitioner's acquired land stood vested in the Gaon Sabha Nangli Sakrawati under Section 81 of the Delhi Land Reforms Act on 22.05.1998, the Petitioner continued to remain in actual cultivatory possession of the acquired land till the date of its acquisition by the Government.
Following the disposal of the apportionment proceedings, the Petitioner made an application for revival of the present reference petition.
Accordingly, vide order dated 23.08.2024, this Court directed the revival of the reference petition.
The LAC, in passing the Award, assessed the market value of the acquired land at Rs. 17,58,400/-
per acre.
The reference petition filed by the Petitioner contends, inter alia, that the LAC's assessment of the market value is grossly inadequate and does not represent the true and fair market value of the land as on the date of the Notification under Section 4 of the Act.
The Ld. LAC assessed the market value based on the policy rates fixed by the Govt. of NCT of Delhi.
a. Ex. PW-1/2 (Sale Deed dated 14.11.2005): This sale deed was executed approximately 4 months and 24 days prior to the date of notification.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
24. The Petitioner has also strongly relied upon the judgment of this Court in the case of R.C. Tehlan v. Union of India (LAC No. 35/2014), wherein the market value for land acquired under the same Notification in the same village was determined.
25. Per contra, the Respondent/Union of India has relied upon the Award (Ex. R1W1/1) and argued that the compensation awarded by the LAC is just and reasonable.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However, it is settled law that when evidence of bona fide sale transactions of the same village and proximate in time is available, the same should be preferred over government minimum rates which often lag behind the actual market trends.
Judicial propriety and the principle of parity demand that owners of acquired lands under the same notification and in the same village for the same block of land should be awarded compensation at a uniform rate, unless there are distinct features distinguishing the lands.
In the present case, no evidence has been led by the Respondents to show that the Petitioner's land is inferior to the land involved in the R.C. Tehlan case or the lands covered by the sale deeds.
Nothing has been brought on record which may prove that the adjudication of the market value in R.C.
Tehlan has been set aside by the Hon'ble Superior Courts.
